comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — prima-deco.pl still shows its cookie-consent modal in the reporter profile because the site builds it from the first-party script /themes/leo_rubik/assets/js/cookieconsent.umd.js; blocking that exact path (verified in the A/B/C experiment:⁠ modal, backdrop and html/body scroll lock gone, page intact) removes the reported annoyance. ## Rule `||prima-deco.pl/themes/leo_rubik/assets/js/cookieconsent.umd.js` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie-consent notice (annoyance), not the site's own advertising, a paywall, or an anti-adblock wall; the run instruction closes none of those categories for it. Filter policy for the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter states that hiding or blocking the corresponding consent scripts is the normal method, so a rule is allowed. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/25026a9205974e56aa63d22e43fe9868e89ffadc/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The gockowiak.pl homepage shows a first-party "Polityka prywatności" cookie-consent modal (`#cookie-modal1`) plus a Bootstrap `.modal-backdrop` that dims the whole storefront; the reporter-profile baseline confirmed both and no existing rule acted on them. A domain-scoped element-hiding rule `gockowiak.pl##.modal-backdrop, #cookie-modal1` verified in the A/B/C experiment (symptom resolved, page integrity intact, scroll preserved). ## Rule `gockowiak.pl##.modal-backdrop, #cookie-modal1` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie/consent notice on a Polish shop, which is the stated purpose of the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter; it is not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, not a German anti-adblock wall, and not an anti-adblock wall of any kind (the page shows no detector and no request to disable the blocker). The instruction's policy rules that close a report (first-party ads, paywalls, German anti-adblock walls, non-reproducible reports) do not apply:⁠ the symptom was reproduced in the reporter-profile session and the fix fits the repository's Cookie Notices rules. Not a scam/phishing/malware page, so the special-case guidance does not apply either. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/25026a9205974e56aa63d22e43fe9868e89ffadc/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Missing information - Traffic eligibility for gockowiak.pl under the filter policy's 100,000 visits/month criterion: The linked AdGuard filter policy requires a site to reach roughly 100,000 visits/month (public statistics or indirect indicators) before a site-specific rule is added. The run has no tool that returns traffic statistics for gockowiak.pl, so this criterion could not be checked; the proposal is made on the observed evidence and the maintainer decides traffic eligibility. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/45090825985 Automated analysis against filters at `25026a9`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.
